rationale: Bound the removed-leader ReadIndex finding with a control for the same cause: the harness now also runs the identical removal in a three-voter cluster, where the reduced configuration has two voters and the singleton shortcut cannot apply. The comparison set retains the single-voter scenario and adds the control's observations, so a future receipt can distinguish the stale immediate answer from the alternative explanation that the removed leader merely keeps operating as a leader for reads. No interpretation is added this turn; the question's account stays as recorded until the receipt exists.

experiment.revision_reason: The harness now also contains the control scenario for the same cause: the identical two-voter removal but with a three-voter cluster, so the reduced configuration has two voters and the singleton shortcut does not apply to the removed leader. The comparison set keeps the earlier scenario and adds the control's observations, so the stale immediate answer can be distinguished from the alternative explanation that the removed leader simply keeps working as a leader for reads.

scope.description: Observe the removed-leader ReadIndex path in two configurations of the same removal: a reduced configuration with a single voter (node 2) and a reduced configuration with two voters (nodes 2 and 3), in both cases after the remaining voters elected a leader and committed a entry the removed leader never receives.
assumptions: Two scenarios in one process: voters {1,2} where the removal leaves {2}, and voters {1,2,3} where the removal leaves {2,3}; ReadOnlySafe and default Config (StepDownOnRemoval false, CheckQuorum false, PreVote false).

In each scenario node 1 is elected leader, the application proposes and applies the committed removal of node 1 on every node, the remaining voters then elect node 2 and commit one entry, and only then is the ReadIndex request delivered to node 1.
Nothing from the current configuration carries a higher term back to node 1, so the removed leader stays at its old term while the observations are taken.
excluded: Check-quorum and pre-vote configurations, which give the removed leader another way to learn that it is stale.
Snapshot transfer and asynchronous storage writes.

experiment.prefix: Scenario A (single-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2}, apply the committed removal of node 1, elect node 2 in {2} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, then deliver the same request to node 2, then run three heartbeat intervals on node 1 and deliver a second MsgReadIndex to node 1. Scenario B (two-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2,3}, apply the committed removal of node 1 on all three nodes, elect node 2 in {2,3} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, then run three heartbeat intervals on node 1 and observe whether any answer is produced.
experiment.requirement: A ReadIndex answer must let the application serve a linearizable read (raft.go:233-244 and README.md:27-32 state that ReadOnlySafe achieves linearizability by communicating with the quorum, and node.go:218-224 states that once the application advances past the returned read index, linearizable reads issued before the request can be processed safely). The tracker's own comment for IsSingleton says the single voting member is the leader, so answering locally without any check is only sound when that member is the local node.
experiment.responsibility: raft (target): the singleton shortcut in the ReadIndex path decides the answer for the whole configuration, and the library already refuses proposals from a leader that is not in its own configuration.

comparisons.description: Scenario A premise: the node whose removal the application applied is still leading a configuration whose single voter is another node.
Scenario A premise: the actual leader of the reduced configuration has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Scenario A witness: the removed leader answered the read with an index below the commit index of the actual leader, sending no message at all.
Scenario A control: the same request answered by the actual leader returns an index that covers its commit index.
Scenario A persistence: after three heartbeat intervals without replies the removed leader repeats the same stale index.
Scenario B premise: the same removal leaves a configuration with two voters, so the singleton shortcut cannot apply to the removed leader (config voters=(2 3)).
Scenario B premise: the new leader of {2,3} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.

Scenario B control outcome: the same read delivered to the removed leader produces no answer at all, and the leader instead enters the readOnly round (heartbeats_emitted 2 with a read context) - the stale immediate answer is specific to the singleton configuration.

Scenario B second symptom: the accepted read stays in readOnly.unconfirmed_reads because the current configuration never acknowledges the removed leader's old-term heartbeats, so no repair exists for it inside raft.
Scenario B persistence: three further heartbeat intervals still produce no answer and no reply from the current configuration.
